claims: The Supreme Court of the United States consists of nine justices.
The Supreme Court of the United States has one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.
Supreme Court justices are nominated by the President.
Supreme Court justices are confirmed by the Senate.
Supreme Court justices hold lifetime tenure.
The current Court is led by Chief Justice John Roberts.
As of April 2026, John G. Roberts, Jr. is Chief Justice.
John G. Roberts, Jr. was nominated by George W. Bush.
John G. Roberts, Jr. took seat in 2005.
Clarence Thomas was nominated by George H.W. Bush.
Clarence Thomas took seat in 1991.
Samuel A. Alito, Jr. was nominated by George W. Bush.
Samuel A. Alito, Jr. took seat in 2006.
Sonia Sotomayor was nominated by Barack Obama.
Sonia Sotomayor took seat in 2009.
Elena Kagan was nominated by Barack Obama.
Elena Kagan took seat in 2010.
Neil M. Gorsuch was nominated by Donald Trump.
Neil M. Gorsuch took seat in 2017.
Brett M. Kavanaugh was nominated by Donald Trump.
Brett M. Kavanaugh took seat in 2018.
Amy Coney Barrett was nominated by Donald Trump.
Amy Coney Barrett took seat in 2020.
Ketanji Brown Jackson was nominated by Joe Biden.
Ketanji Brown Jackson took seat in 2022.
Clarence Thomas is the longest serving justice since 1991.
Ketanji Brown Jackson is the most recent appointment in 2022.
All current justices attended law school.
Several current justices graduated from Harvard or Yale.
The Supreme Court is the final arbiter in federal legal cases.
The Supreme Court is responsible for interpreting the Constitution.
